title: A new view of the Helix Nebula
credit: NASA, ESA, C.R. O'Dell (Vanderbilt University), and M. Meixner, P. McCullough, and G. Bacon (Space Telescope Science Institute)

geometryEvidence.reference: The picture lies on two tilted planes through the central star (recipe geometry.rings; https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0407556); the recipe's own inclination is not used.

registration.method: What the publisher's page prints, used as it is: the frame's centre at 22 29 41.92, -20 50 13.29, a field of 27.26 by 29.38 arcmin, north 0.3° left of vertical. Checked here against the archive's own Hubble F658N mosaic of the nebula: the centre agrees to 0.1 arcsec; the picture's north-south scale is 0.9% smaller than the printed field gives and its axes are 0.1° and 0.9° left of vertical, so a point at the frame's edge is up to 7 arcsec from where the tags put it.

displayModel: The picture's light lies on two tilted planes through the central star: an inner disc of radius 250 arcsec tilted 23 degrees and the plane of the outer ring, radius 371 arcsec, tilted 53 degrees about another axis. Inside the disc's radius a sight line's light is on the disc, beyond the ring's radius on the ring's plane; between the two radii the planes share it in proportion. Which plane holds a patch of light there is not measured. Each structure is about 100 arcsec deep along the sight line: the smooth part of its light is a glow of that depth about its plane, and the rest, with every detail, lies on the plane.
coverage: The published frame inside a circle of 770 arcsec about the central star, fading out over its last 7%. The stars Gaia lists in the field are removed before the bake, all but the central star; fainter stars and background galaxies remain, on the nebula's planes whatever their own distances.

acquisition.operation: Download the publisher's JPEG; no crop or resample.
